Article Title: 'Purity of voter list': Yogi Adityanath defends SIR after 'missing' Hindu voters claim
Article Text:
Yogi Adityanath has staunchly defended the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, emphasizing its role in maintaining the integrity of voter lists.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday defended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls amid a political row over his claim that 1.27 crore Hindu voters were missing from the state's electoral rolls. The CM backed the SIR process and asserted that the exercise was necessary to ensure the "purity" of voter lists.At News18 Rising Bharat Summit, Yogi Adityanath said the names of deceased persons and non-citizens should be removed from electoral rolls, while every eligible adult Indian citizen must be included. He also said the BJP workers would ensure that no eligible voter was left out and expressed confidence that the exercise would be conducted transparently."The names of voters who have passed away should be removed from the electoral rolls. The names of people who are not citizens of India should not be included in the electoral rolls. Every adult Indian citizen should have their name included in the voter list," he said.His remarks come a day after Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa clarified that the Election Commission's database does not maintain information on voters' religion or caste.Rinwa said the poll body could not officially classify missing voters on religious lines and ruled out any conspiracy to target a particular community.Earlier, Yogi Adityanath had claimed that 1.27 crore Hindu voters were missing from the electoral rolls after the SIR. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had questioned the source of the chief minister's figures.Targeting the Congress over its allegations of vote theft and questions about the SIR and Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), Yogi Adityanath said the party blamed constitutional institutions for its electoral failures."When they win, it is their victory, but when they lose, the EVM is wrong, the SIR is wrong, and the Election Commission is responsible," he said, accusing the Congress of undermining constitutional institutions.Taking a swipe at Rahul Gandhi, he alleged that the Congress leader became part of every campaign that was against India's interests or questioned its constitutional institutions."Unfortunately, there is still a lack of maturity. He should avoid such frivolous issues and speak on merit, facts and evidence," the CM said.Responding to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's remarks about adding another 'P' for 'Pandits' to his broader social coalition of "PDA", amid perceptions of discontent among Brahmins, Adityanath cited statements by some SP leaders and said their remarks and the party's past conduct towards Hindu communities reflected its actual position.Speaking at the News18 event, Yogi Adityanath also expressed confidence in the BJP's return to power in the 2027 assembly elections.Asked whether the BJP-led NDA would cross its target of 320 seats in the 403-member assembly, the chief minister said the party would receive public support, but stopped short of giving a direct numerical assurance."Ask any woman, youth, trader or poor person, and they will say the government should return to power. Those who dislike development, see negativity in every initiative and want an atmosphere of disorder will be disappointed," he said.Later, reacting to Yogi Adityanath's confidence that the BJP would win more than 320 seats, Congress leader Pawan Khera said: "Will they get 320 seats? Isn't this 100 seats short? But who will be the CM? He (Adityanath) alleges that Hindu votes have been cut. If they are still getting 320 seats, it means there has been some agreement and they know what will happen," Khera said.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath says names of deceased persons and non-citizens should be removed from electoral rolls. Uttar Pradesh chief minister says every eligible adult Indian citizen must be included. He also expressed confidence in the BJP's return to power in the 2027 assembly elections.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday called the newly formed alliance between AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party president Chandrashekhar Aazad the "B team" of the Samajwadi Party and Congress.He alleged that the opposition parties had brought the two leaders together to damage the BJP ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.According to news agency PTI, speaking at the News18 Rising Bharat Summit: North Edition in Lucknow, Adityanath said the Samajwadi Party was attempting to pursue two political strategies simultaneously by bringing Owaisi and Chandrashekhar together."The Samajwadi Party has now started riding two boats, and we know that riding two boats ultimately leads to sinking. Keeping this possibility in mind, it has brought together the Hyderabad 'maulana' and Chandrashekhar so that they can create an atmosphere here," he said.This was Adityanath's first public reaction to the Samajik Parivartan Morcha, launched by Owaisi and Chandrashekhar in Lucknow on November 12. The two leaders have announced plans to jointly contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, aiming to prevent the BJP from returning to power for a third consecutive term.The alliance has positioned itself as a political platform for marginalised communities, including Dalits, minorities and backward sections, and has invited the Samajwadi Party, Congress and other opposition parties to join its effort to defeat the BJP.Targeting the Samajwadi Party over its appeal among Dalit voters, Adityanath alleged that the party had disrespected the community and its prominent personalities."Dalits do not want to look towards the Samajwadi Party because of the disrespect it has shown towards them and their great personalities. This is an attempt to damage the BJP and other parties," he said.Taking a swipe at Owaisi, Adityanath said, "I assure the Hyderabad maulana that when he leaves from here, he will remember that when a government is formed in Uttar Pradesh, Hyderabad will become Bhagya Lakshmi Puram."Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav had welcomed the formation of the new front, saying it could cost the BJP two to three per cent of votes. However, he maintained that his party's alliance with the Congress under the INDIA bloc would continue.The alliance brings together two leaders seeking to expand their political influence among Muslim and Dalit voters in Uttar Pradesh.While Owaisi heads the AIMIM, Chandrashekhar leads the Azad Samaj Party and has built his political identity around Dalit rights and representation.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath called the newly formed alliance between AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party president Chandrashekhar Aazad the "B team" of the Samajwadi Party and Congress. The two leaders have announced plans to jointly contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.

Article Title: Plea alleges Sonia Gandhi used forged papers for 1980 voter entry; court seeks police report
Article Text:
Court seeks Delhi Police report on plea alleging Sonia Gandhi's name in voter list before citizenship

How the case reached the ACJM court

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the courts have more power in handling electoral complaints? Yes, definitely No, existing powers are sufficient 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Rouse Avenue Court on Wednesday sought an Action Taken Report (ATR) from the station house officer (SHO) of Delhi's IP Estate Police Station on complaint alleging that senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi 's name was included in the electoral rolls before she acquired Indian citizenship in April 1983.Additional chief judicial magistrate (ACJM) Vinod Joshi issued the direction on a complaint filed by advocate Vikas Tripathi on August 24, 2025. The court has scheduled the next hearing for November 28.During Wednesday's proceedings, the complainant submitted attested copies of the electoral rolls for 1980, 1981 and 1983. However, the court directed him to place the original attested copies of the voter lists on record.Senior advocate Ajay Burman appeared on behalf of Tripathi.The complaint alleges that Sonia Gandhi's name featured in the electoral roll in 1980, nearly three years before she acquired Indian citizenship in April 1983. It raises questions over the alleged inclusion of her name in the voter lists during a period when she was not an Indian citizen.The court had earlier, on November 11, allowed the complainant to submit additional documents in support of his allegations.The proceedings follow a remand by the Session Court, which sent the matter back to the ACJM court for fresh consideration.The Session Court had set aside a 2025 order by the magistrate refusing to direct the registration of an FIR against Sonia Gandhi.On September 21, Special Judge (MP-MLA cases) Vishal Gogne allowed a revision petition filed by Tripathi challenging the Magistrate's order.While setting aside the earlier order, the Sessions Court observed that the complaint had been rejected on the basis of photocopies of unverified records."The order is an non speaking order. It is liable to be set aside," Special Judge Gogne had observed.The revisional court also questioned the magistrate's observations on the jurisdiction of the Central Government and the Election Commission in matters relating to citizenship.It held that the findings concerning the roles of these authorities in the citizenship issue were improper. The Sessions Court further noted that the earlier order did not adequately explain whether the complaint disclosed the commission of a cognisable offence.Referring to the allegations and documents submitted by the complainant, the Sessions Court noted that Sonia Gandhi's name was allegedly included in the electoral roll in 1980, removed in 1982 and added again in 1983.The court also pointed out that electoral rolls are meant for Indian citizens and referred to documents submitted by the complainant that allegedly listed Sonia Gandhi's name alongside her residential address at Safdarjung Road in New Delhi.However, the Sessions Court clarified that it could not assume the role of the Magistrate and decide the complaint itself. It remanded the matter for fresh consideration, directing the magistrate to seek a status report from the concerned police officer and pass a reasoned order after hearing the officer.The matter is now before the ACJM court in accordance with the Sessions Court's directions. The allegations against Sonia Gandhi remain part of the complaint and are yet to be adjudicated.
Article Summary: Court seeks Delhi Police report on plea alleging Sonia Gandhi's name in voter list before citizenship. Court seeks an Action Taken Report (ATR) from the station house officer (SHO) of Delhi's IP Estate Police Station. Complaint alleges that senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's name was included in the electoral rolls before she acquired Indian citizenship in April 1983.

Article Title: 'Who ransacked Halebidu?' BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi over Hoysaleshwara Temple post
Article Text:
‘Who ransacked Halebidu?' BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday hit back at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks that fear, anger and hatred had created a web in the hearts of BJP and RSS supporters, asking him to identify those responsible for the destruction of the historic Hoysala capital of Halebidu in Karnataka.Responding to Rahul's post on X, the BJP questioned his use of the phrase “Satyam Shivam Sundaram” and referred to the history of the Hoysala capital, which was ransacked during invasions in the 14th century.“Mr Gandhi, since you've posted Halebidu, a few questions,” the party said while retweeting his post.The BJP asked Rahul whether he knew why Dwarasamudra, the former Hoysala capital, came to be known as Halebidu, meaning the "old capital”.“Can you bring yourself to name who ransacked it? We can: Alauddin Khalji's general Malik Kafur in 1311, and Muhammad bin Tughlaq's army in 1326-27. Can you shame them?” the party said.Referring to the damaged sculptures at the Hoysaleshwara Temple complex, it added, “Across Halebidu, Idols of gods still stand with broken faces and hands. Who broke them?”“Satyam comes first in Satyam Shivam Sundaram, RaGa. Did you know?” the BJP added.The exchange followed Rahul's post on X earlier on Tuesday, in which he hit back at BJP and RSS supporters amid the controversy over his remarks about his parents' relationship. He said fear, anger and hatred had prevented them from experiencing and expressing love.“Fear, anger and hatred have woven a web in the hearts of BJP and RSS supporters that stops them from experiencing and expressing love,” the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha said.“As a true Hindu, it is my duty to free them from this web, so that they too can start to experience the breathtaking beauty and joy of love and belonging in their lives,” he added, ending his post with “Satyam Shivam Sundaram”.The sculpture at the Hoysaleshwara Temple in Halebidu that Rahul referred to depicts Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati riding Nandi, Shiva's sacred bull.Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma also criticised Rahul's post, saying no human being, including anyone from the Gandhi family, could be equated with God."To portray mortals as Shiv and Parvati is not devotion. It is entitlement grown so arrogant that it believes itself divine," Sarma said in a post on X.He added that people should bow before God rather than equate themselves with Him, stressing that humility was the foundation of greatness.The political row comes a day after Rahul's remarks about his parents, Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi, at the launch of his mother's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love.Recalling his childhood at the event, Rahul said his mother would sit in his father's lap during lunch and dinner.“For every meal, there’d be Papa and in Papa’s lap there would be Mumma,” he said, adding that he had considered it normal until he visited his friends' homes and noticed that their parents did not display similar affection.
Article Summary: BJP asks Rahul Gandhi to identify those responsible for the destruction of the historic Hoysala capital of Halebidu in Karnataka. The exchange followed Rahul's post on X earlier on Tuesday, in which he hit back at BJP and RSS supporters amid the controversy over his remarks about his parents' relationship.

Article Title: SC to hear INDIA bloc's poser plea on CEC on Dec 9
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Senior advocates Kapil Sibal and AM Singhvi Tuesday tried to persuade Supreme Court to issue notice on INDIA bloc members' plea to serve a 48-question 'interrogatory' on CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi but failed in their endeavour.As a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana ran out of time to hear in detail the new 'interrogatory' plea of bloc members led by Rahul Gandhi and was adjourning the hearing to Dec 9, Sibal and Singhvi kept persuading SC to issue notice on the application or in the alternative seek response from CEC and ECs, even though both options meant the same.There is no question of filing any response to the application," said Election Commission counsel - senior advocates Harish Salve and Maninder Singh."It will save time of the court," said Sibal and Singhvi trying to impress upon the top court that the 'interrogatory' was an essential part of discovering facts in the unanimous and joint affidavit filed by CEC and ECs in response to the petition filed by the INDIA bloc's members alleging irregularities in pan-India SIR and undemocratic functioning of the poll panel.The CJI-led bench asked whether pleadings are complete in the bunch of petitions in addition to the one filed by Rahul and other opposition leaders, and said it is just adjourning the hearing to Dec 9.Also Read| Jantar Mantar protest nod denied due to CJP past conduct: Cops in SC When the two senior advocate-turned opposition MPs renewed their request for seeking response on the 'interrogatory' application, the bench said, "We are not issuing notice today. We are simply adjourning the case. We will hear arguments on the (maintainability) of the 'interrogatory' application (on Dec 9) and then decide whether to issue notice or not."The interrogatory application was filed in the joint writ petition by Rahul and other opposition politicians, including Mallikarjun Kharge, TMC's Saugata Roy, SP supremo Akhilesh Yadav, RJD chief Tejashwi Yadav, Sena UBT's Sanjay Raut, CPM's M A Baby, CPI's D Raja, JMM's Mahua Majhi, NCP's Supriya Sule and IUML's E T Mohammed Basheer.They have sought the suspension of SIR and permitting the inclusion of eligible voters in the electoral rolls of Punjab and other poll-bound states.Invoking interrogatory procedure, which is a commonly used tool under Civil Procedure Code to seek clarity on assertions of the opposite party, the opposition leaders said, "Each 'interrogatory' is to be answered separately and fully. Where any fact is not known or not recorded, the answer shall say so expressly and identify the person or record from whom or from which it could be ascertained."The opposition gave a brief outline of the 48 questions in the 'interrogatory': "Whether particular decisions were taken by the commission acting as a body; when and in what manner they were taken; who authorised particular actions in the name of the commission; and how ECINET has been designed, altered and operated."
Article Summary: Senior advocates Kapil Sibal and AM Singhvi tried to persuade Supreme Court to issue notice on INDIA bloc members' plea to serve a 48-question 'interrogatory' on CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana adjourned the hearing to Dec 9.

Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. Article Title: Deshmukh retains Latur DCC Bank as Congress-backed panel wins 14 of 19 seats, Mahayuti secures just 5 amid rift within alliance
Article Text:
Former Congress MLA Dhiraj Deshmukh during the victory rally on Monday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

Congress-backed Sahakar Panel has decisively retained control of Latur District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank, winning 14of the 19 director seats and handing Mahayuti-backed Parivartan Panel a resounding defeat in one of Marathwada’s most closely watched cooperative battles.Led by former Congress MLA Dhiraj Deshmukh, son of the late chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh , Sahakar Panel secured 10 of the 15 seats contested on Monday. The tally added to four directors who had already been elected unopposed, cementing the panel’s dominance. The campaign was guided by veteran politician Diliprao Deshmukh and bolstered by a cross-party understanding with cooperation minister Babasaheb Patil, a factor widely seen as crucial to the outcome.For Dhiraj Deshmukh, the victory marks a significant political comeback after his defeat in the 2024 assembly elections. “We could reach out to voters with our work done in the past. For every criticism of opposition, we focused on showcasing our performance,” he said.Emphasising that cooperative elections should not be viewed through a purely political lens, Deshmukh said he was willing to work with opposition-backed directors for the welfare of farmers and the development of Latur.The result is a major setback for Mahayuti, which had fielded its top local leadership in a bid to wrest control of the cooperative institution. BJP MLAs Sambhaji Patil Nilangekar, Ramesh Karad and Abhimanyu Pawar, along with NCP MLA Sanjay Bansode, campaigned extensively for Parivartan Panel. The alliance, however, managed to secure just five seats.The lone highlight for Mahayuti came in the Nilanga Society constituency, where BJP state secretary Arvind Patil Nilangekar (brother of Sambhaji Patil Nilangekar) defeated his aunt in a closely watched family contest. Arvind alleged that the rival camp had resorted to unfair tactics, including the rejection of nomination forms of opposition candidates. “Despite the challenges, we have established a foothold in the DCC Bank. Our representation may be small, but it will be sufficient to ensure checks and balances in the bank’s functioning,” he said.The election also exposed fault lines within Mahayuti in Marathwada. Cooperation minister Babasaheb Patil’s decision to align with the Deshmukh camp instead of BJP nominee is believed to have weakened the alliance’s campaign on the ground and contributed significantly to the Congress-backed panel’s victory.The high-stakes contest recorded an impressive 99.4% turnout, with 993 of the 999 eligible voters casting their ballots on Sunday.The outcome assumes added significance as it comes months after the 2024 Maharashtra assembly elections, in which Mahayuti won five of Latur district’s six seats and BJP emerged as the dominant force with victories in Latur Rural, Nilanga and Ausa. The DCC Bank result is likely to be viewed within BJP ranks as a warning sign that the party has yet to translate its assembly poll success into control of key cooperative institutions in the district.
Article Summary: Congress-backed Sahakar Panel has decisively retained control of Latur District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank. The result is a major setback for Mahayuti, which had fielded its top local leadership in a bid to wrest control of the cooperative institution.

The crime branch unit-I of Nashik city police arrested 13 people and seized cash and gambling materials worth Rs 3.4 lakh after busting an illegal gambling racket operating near Nashik Road railway station.Police said constables Sandeep Bhand and Uttam Pawar received confidential information on Nov 13 that a group — led by Santosh Gudne, Bhurya Mamu alias Firoz, Ashfaq Shaikh, Shabbir and Hussain — was targeting people around the railway station by promising to double their money. The accused allegedly lured passengers arriving at the station into games such as Teen Patti and Kala Pila and cheated them using various tricks.Based on the tip-off, senior inspector Anchal Mudgal deployed multiple teams led by sub-inspector Ramiz Shaikh in plain clothes at the railway station, bus stand, nearby hotels and surrounding areas.During the operation, the teams raided the spot and nabbed 13 suspects. All the accused are from outside Nashik, mainly Mumbai and Thane, police said.Police seized cash and gambling-related materials collectively valued at Rs 3.4 lakh from the accused. A case has been registered at Nashik Road police station under cheating charges and the provisions of the Maharashtra Prevention of Gambling Act. Further investigation is being carried out by the crime branch unit-I.
Article Summary: The crime branch unit-I of Nashik city police arrested 13 people and seized cash and gambling materials worth Rs 3.4 lakh. The accused allegedly lured passengers arriving at the station into games such as Teen Patti and Kala Pila and cheated them using various tricks.

CHENNAI: St Thomas Mount police registered a case against YouTuber and Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) functionary ‘Saattai’ Duraimurugan for allegedly making defamatory remarks linking Meenakshi, arrested in the Madurai Tanishq jewellery showroom robbery case, to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).The case was registered based on a complaint filed by Nandakumar, a TVK functionary from Alandur.He stated that Duraimurugan uploaded a video on his YouTube channel on November 14, claiming that Meenakshi was associated with TVK.In his complaint, Nandakumar said Meenakshi had no connection with the party and accused Duraimurugan of spreading false information that tarnished its reputation.Based on the complaint, St Thomas Mount police registered a case under three sections, including provisions relating to intentional provocation with the intent to cause a breach of public peace.

A 33-year-old employee of a news channel fell to his death from the third floor of a party hall in Jafferkhanpet while celebrating a friend’s birthday on Monday night. He reportedly lost his balance while leaning against a window.The deceased was identified as Anbumani, a native of Edappadi in Salem district, who was working in Chennai. He was employed in the marketing department of a news channel. Police said Anbumani and his friends rented the hall in Jafferkhanpet to celebrate his friend Santosh’s birthday. During the celebration, Anbumani lit candles on the birthday cake and moved towards a window, lost balance and fell from the third floor and died.On receiving information, MGR Nagar police rushed to the scene, recovered the body, and sent it to ESI Hospital for postmortem. Investigators also found that the incident had been captured in a video recorded during the birthday party.A case of accidental death has been registered, and police are questioning Anbumani’s friends. They ruled out foul play in the incident. An investigating officer said that the window had sliding glass panels but no protective grill.

Article Title: Rash and wrong-side driving: Coimbatore district police book driver, seize private bus, recommend cancellation of licence and permit
Article Text:

COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore district police have seized a private mofussil bus and booked its driver for rash, negligent and wrong-side driving at Pappampatti Pirivu on the Coimbatore–Palladam Road.According to a statement issued by the district police on Tuesday, the incident occurred around 8.30am on Monday while the private bus was heading to Coimbatore from Tirupur. Near Pappampatti Pirivu, which falls under the Sulur police station limits, driver Sakthivel drove the bus at a high speed before abruptly swerving the vehicle to the right and driving against the oncoming traffic on the wrong side of the busy stretch, putting motorists and pedestrians at a grave risk.Several commuters recorded the dangerous manoeuvre and uploaded the footage online, where it quickly gained widespread traction. Acting on a formal complaint lodged by a motorist, the Sulur police registered a case against Sakthivel under Section 281 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) read with Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act Police impounded the bus and parked it on the Sulur police station premises for further legal proceedings. Additionally, authorities have written to the regional transport officer recommending the cancellation of Sakthivel’s driving licence as well as the vehicle’s route permit.Reiterating a zero-tolerance stance, the district police warned that strict legal action would be taken against motorists endangering public safety.
Article Summary: The Coimbatore district police seized a private mofussil bus and booked its driver for rash, negligent and wrong-side driving. Driver Sakthivel drove the bus at a high speed before abruptly swerving the vehicle to the right and driving against the oncoming traffic.

Article Title: Verdict on Sulur minor girl rape-murder case postponed to Nov 27
Article Text: COIMBATORE: A special court for Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act cases on Monday postponed to Nov 27 its verdict on the rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl near Sulur in Coimbatore district.The verdict was scheduled to be pronounced on Monday by judge Hariharan. No specific reason was stated for the postponement.On May 21, a 10-year-old girl from Pallapalayam near Sulur went missing after visiting a local shop. Her body was found the next day near the Kannampalayam lakebed. Police arrested K Karthi,35, and R Mohan, 31, both of whom were residing in the same locality.Police registered a case under sections 5(m), 5(i), 6(1), 5(I), 5(j)(iv), 16 and 17 of the POCSO Act and 103(1), 61(2)(a), 140(1), 140(4), 238(a), 127(2), 65, 49, 240, 249(a) of the BNS. The first hearing of the case took place on June 10. Prime accused Karthi was lodged in Madurai Central Prison, while Mohan was lodged in Trichy Central Prison.On Monday, both were produced before the court. While police were bringing them to the court, Mohan asked the media people not to take video of him, claiming that police had falsely included him in the case.
Article Summary: The verdict was scheduled to be pronounced on Monday by judge Hariharan. No specific reason was stated for the postponement. On May 21, a 10-year-old girl from Pallapalayam near Sulur went missing after visiting a local shop. Her body was found the next day near the Kannampalayan lakebed.

Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. A police inspector who was suspended following a sexual harassment complaint by a woman colleague has been dismissed from service for remaining absent from duty for 555 consecutive days without permission during an earlier posting.S N Thileeban, formerly attached to Arumuganeri police station in Tuticorin district, was removed from service by Tirunelveli range deputy inspector general of police Thirunavukkarasu following a departmental inquiry. The dismissal order has been served on him.According to police, Thileeban was serving as a sub-inspector at Arumanai police station in Kanyakumari district in 2023 and was on deputation to the economic offences wing in Chennai. During this period, he remained absent for 555 days without obtaining prior permission or informing his superiors.He also failed to appear before a medical board as directed. During the departmental inquiry, he neither cooperated with the proceedings nor submitted an explanation for his prolonged absence, prompting disciplinary action.In June this year, Thileeban was suspended after a woman police officer at Arumuganeri accused him of sexual harassment. He subsequently released videos on Instagram denying the allegations, claiming that he had never harassed female personnel. He also expressed willingness to cooperate with the investigation.The latest dismissal stems from his unauthorised absence during an earlier posting and is unrelated to the sexual harassment complaint.

Article Title: Custodial death: HC directs state to preserve CCTV footage at four police stations
Article Text:
Custodial death: HC directs state to preserve CCTV footage at four police stations

Cleared/300 Words Madras high court on Tuesday directed the state to preserve the CCTV footage at Checkanurani, Valandur, Usilampatti Town and Usilampatti Taluk police stations in Madurai district and submit a copy of the same, while hearing a plea pertaining to the death of a man in police custody in Checkanurani police station.Justice D Lingeswaran passed the order while hearing the petition filed by B Sudha, wife of the deceased truck driver R Balakrishnan of Theni district.The petitioner stated that her husband was employed with a Madurai-based delivery company. While he was driving a truck loaded with cardamom along Thevaram-Madurai route, the vehicle caught fire near Valandur cremation ground on Usilampatti-Theni Road. Her husband tried to put out the fire and also recorded a video of it on his mobile phone. The goods were destroyed in the fire. Thereafter, he went to Valandur police station and lodged a complaint.She stated that her husband informed the truck owner about this incident, who asked him to go to Checkanurani police station. Her husband was questioned by the police personnel and was taken to Valandur and Usilampatti police stations. He was kept at Checkanurani police station beyond midnight. She was then informed that her husband had died by suicide.Sudha said her husband died in police custody solely due to the torture and ill-treatment at the hands of Checkanurani police, causing his severe physical and mental suffering.The petitioner stated that the postmortem revealed that her husband had suffered physical torture at the hands of the police prior to his death. Police claimed that her husband hanged himself inside the station toilet. CCTV footage was the only independent means by which the police version could be tested. Hence, the petitioner moved the court seeking preservation of CCTV footage at the four police stations.
Article Summary: Madras high court orders state to preserve CCTV footage at four police stations. Hearing a plea pertaining to the death of a man in police custody in Checkanurani police station. Wife of the deceased truck driver R Balakrishnan of Theni district said her husband had suffered physical torture at the hands of the police.

SALEM: A govt school teacher was arrested in Salem district on Sunday night under sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act on charges of inappropriate behaviour towards girl students.The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district.According to the complaint, the teacher allegedly made inappropriate remarks to Class X girl students on Nov 5. “He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’ while commenting on the beauty of her eyes,” said an officer at the all women police station in Attur.The students brought the matter to the notice of the headmaster on Nov 13. The headmaster informed chief educational officer A Ellappan and contacted Childline 1098 seeking intervention.Following the complaint, a member of the child welfare committee visited the school on Nov 14 and conducted an inquiry into the allegations raised by the students.Based on the findings, the headmaster lodged a complaint with the Attur all women police on Sunday. Police registered a case against Sankar and arrested him. He was remanded in judicial custody.

Article Title: ACB arrests six officials in Rims land scam case
Article Text:
ACB said it had found evidence of criminal conspiracy and misuse of official positions for personal financial gain

Ranchi:

Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested six govt officials in connection with the alleged illegal registration and mutation of land belonging to Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences (Rims), and its conversion into private holdings.In a statement issued on Tuesday evening, ACB identified the accused as former land records deputy collector Manoj Kumar Ranjan; former sub-registrars of Ranchi district Avinash Kumar, Vaibhavmani Tripathi and Rahul Kumar Choubey; and former Bargain and Sadar circle officers Sailesh Kumar and Rajesh Kumar, respectively.The bureau said it had found evidence of criminal conspiracy and misuse of official positions for personal financial gain. “Further legal action is being taken against them,” it said.ACB registered the case on Jan 5 under various sections of BNS and the Prevention of Corruption Act, following directions from Jharkhand high court.According to the FIR, the case relates to the alleged registration and mutation of land through a criminal conspiracy aimed at bypassing rules and converting govt property into private land.The district administration had earlier carried out large-scale demolitions of buildings constructed on the allegedly illegally transferred land. Work is currently underway to build a boundary wall around the property.
Article Summary: Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested six govt officials in connection with the alleged illegal registration and mutation of land. Accused are former land records deputy collector Manoj Kumar Ranjan; former sub-registrars of Ranchi district Avinash Kumar, Vaibhavmani Tripathi and Rahul Kumar Choubey.
